papers.title: Synergistic effects of TC4 and heat treatment on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and high-temperature oxidation properties of laser-deposited GH4169 alloys
papers.abstract: This study systematically investigates the synergistic effects of Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) addition and homogenization plus dual aging (HA) heat treatment on the microstructure, tensile properties, and high-temperature oxidation resistance of GH4169 alloys fabricated via laser melting deposition (LMD). Microstructural analysis demonstrates that TC4 addition reduces grain size and Laves phase length, while HA treatment promotes δ-Ni3Nb phase precipitation and Laves phase dissolution. Crystallographic orientation analysis reveals a coherent relationship between γ and γ′ phases, but an incoherent relationship between γ and γ″ phases. Tensile tests indicate that HA treatment not only enhances tensile strength but also improves the elongation of the 5TC4/GH4169 composite, yielding a 45% increase in yield strength (from 738 MPa to 1070 MPa) and a 28% rise in elongation (from 17.5% to 22.4%). This improvement is primarily attributed to precipitation strengthening and dislocation strengthening mediated by finer γ′ and γ″ precipitates. High-temperature oxidation tests at 800°C show that the synergy of TC4 and HA treatment reduces mass gain by 9% (from 0.45 mg·cm<sup>-2</sup> to 0.41 mg·cm<sup>-2</sup>) and lowers the oxidation rate to 1.99 × 10-8 mg<sup>2</sup>·cm<sup>-4</sup>·s<sup>-1</sup>, indicating enhanced oxidation resistance due to a continuous Nb<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>-TiO<sub>2</sub>-NiO-Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> oxide layer. These findings highlight the efficacy of TC4 reinforcement and tailored thermal processing in optimizing Ni-based alloys for additive manufacturing applications.
papers.venue: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

papers.title: Cooling and Lubrication Strategies for Internal Grinding of Ti-6Al-4V: A Review with Emphasis on MQL-Cold CO₂ Hybrid Cooling
papers.abstract: Ti-6Al-4V is a difficult-to-machine material due to its low thermal conductivity, low elastic modulus, and high chemical reactivity at machining temperatures. These characteristics lead to significant heat generation during grinding, increased friction, material adhesion to the wheel (clogging), and degradation of surface integrity. These challenges become even more severe in internal grinding, where the confined machining zone restricts the delivery of coolants/lubricants to the contact area and complicates local thermal control. This paper provides a comprehensive review of cooling and lubrication strategies for the internal grinding of Ti-6Al-4V, with a focus on MQL/SQL (Minimum/Small Quantity Lubrication), cryogenic cooling, and hybrid configurations. Experimental results indicate that liquid nitrogen (LN2) cooling can reduce tangential grinding forces by 8–27%, normal grinding forces by 3–12%, surface roughness by up to 38%, and grinding zone temperatures by 55% when machining Ti-6Al-4V. Furthermore, research on titanium grinding demonstrates that SQL combined with liquid CO2 improves grindability more effectively than dry grinding or the use of CO2 alone. Based on the published literature, a single optimal method for the internal grinding of Ti-6Al-4V has not yet been definitively established. However, the integration of MQL with chilled CO2 represents a promising solution due to its potential to provide simultaneous lubrication and effective heat dissipation.

summary_en.motivation: The poor thermal conductivity and high chemical reactivity of Ti-6Al-4V cause severe grinding challenges, especially in confined internal grinding, necessitating a review of cooling and lubrication strategies.
summary_en.method: This review systematically analyzes multiple cooling/lubrication approaches for internal grinding of Ti-6Al-4V, including MQL/SQL, cryogenic cooling (LN2, CO2), and hybrid configurations.
summary_en.result: No single optimal method is established, but MQL combined with chilled CO2 shows promise for balancing lubrication and heat dissipation.
summary_en.validation: The review aggregates experimental findings from previous studies without presenting new experimental data.
